analysis.investment_thesis: IndiaMART is India's dominant B2B marketplace with genuine network effects — buyers attract sellers and vice versa, making displacement extremely difficult. At 21.6x earnings with 27% ROE, virtually zero debt, and INR 615 Cr of free cash flow growing at a healthy clip, the price is fair for the quality of this franchise.
key_strengths: Powerful two-sided network moat: 100M+ registered buyers create a self-reinforcing competitive advantage that is very hard to replicate
Exceptional capital efficiency: ROE 26.9%, ROCE 34.2%, Debt/Equity 0.01, and capex of only INR 8 Cr in 2025 on revenues of INR 1,388 Cr — this is as asset-light as it gets
Consistent and growing free cash flow: OCF positive all 5 years, FCF grew from INR 256 Cr (2020) to INR 615 Cr (2025), with operating margins expanding to 31.6%
key_risks: Revenue growth has moderated to ~15% CAGR in recent years and is slowing, raising questions about market saturation among India's SME segment
Other income (INR 272 Cr in 2025) now constitutes ~50% of net profit — the business is partly functioning as a treasury operation, masking core earnings quality
Competition from Amazon Business, Google, and vertical-specific B2B platforms could erode pricing power on supplier subscriptions
red_flags: Promoter stake of 49.12% is adequate but not dominant — watch for any dilution or secondary sales
Heavy reliance on investment income inflates reported profits; core operating earnings alone would show a higher true P/E
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IndiaMART is a textbook Buffett-style network-effects business: it connects India's 60-million-strong SME universe through a marketplace where scale begets more scale. Revenue has compounded at 20.8% over nine years while capital expenditure remains negligible (INR 8 Cr in FY25), resulting in extraordinary FCF conversion. The operating margin of 31.6% and near-zero debt load mean this business can fund its own growth and return capital to shareholders without ever needing to knock on a banker's door.

The valuation at 21.6x trailing earnings is reasonable — not a screaming bargain, but fair for a franchise of this quality in a large, underpenetrated market. The main caution is that roughly half of reported profits come from treasury income on a large cash pile; strip that out and the business is still well-priced but less dramatically cheap. At the current price, this is a good business at a fair price — exactly the kind of opportunity I seek.
